A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and provide readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Retained content and the additions in v2 can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original network simulations, geometric analyses, and warping interventions, including the experimental MSE comparison in S8.3.

after.justification: v2 retains those results and adds original analyses of a parametric working-memory RNN and a state-space model trained on human BCI recordings in S8.5–S8.6.

M1.justification: The central pullback-metric framework is unchanged. The added applications introduce a scalar-comparison RNN objective in S8.5 and a one-layer HiPPO (LegS) linear state-space model with a cursor-reconstruction objective in S8.6, constituting limited model and training extensions.

E1.justification: v2 retains the synthetic network tasks and adds sequential scalar-magnitude comparison through the Romo task, plus offline cursor decoding from a human participant's BCI recordings. S8.5–S8.6 substantially broaden task requirements and extend coverage to recorded neural data.

E2.justification: S8.3 retains the same five comparison conditions: Untrained model, Baseline trained model, No warping, Untrained W, and Only warping-trained W. The new applications introduce no evaluated competing baselines; HiPPO is the analyzed model in S8.6.

E3.justification: The existing protocols are retained, while two distinct experimental designs are added. S8.5 specifies timed scalar stimuli, delayed classification, and stable-rank tracking. S8.6 introduces offline neural-data decoding with constructed cursor targets and spline interpolation across line lengths.

E4.justification: Figures S10–S11 add substantive mechanistic case studies: whether sequential scalar memories separate during retention and collapse during decision-making, and whether movement length relates to trajectory speed. Existing activation-function comparisons, warping interventions, and delay analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Figure S10 adds explicitly defined 20th–80th percentile bands for the two output regions, whereas the retained working-memory analysis uses 10th–90th percentiles. Existing uncertainty reports remain unchanged, and v2 supplies no new seed or repeated-run counts.

E6.justification: New results show dimensional expansion during Romo-task retention followed by contraction toward one dimension, and movement-dependent alignment of time and length tangent vectors in the BCI model. Matched existing results remain unchanged, including every MSE entry in S8.3.

T1.justification: Existing numbered theorems and proofs are retained. S7.2 adds finite-time/asymptotic qualifications and a chaos argument, while S8.5 adds a subtraction-map pullback calculation. That calculation is inconsistent as written: its orthogonal-vector assumption implies zero cross terms, unlike the displayed matrix.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same claims about input-constrained topology, pullback geometry, and dynamic warping during computation. The appendix additions provide further support without redefining those headline claims.

C2.justification: S7.2 newly distinguishes transient manifolds from asymptotic attractors and discusses chaotic stretching. S8.5 interprets the new geometry through subtraction and binarization; S8.6 links tangent alignment to faster trajectories for longer movements. Existing connectivity-degeneracy and pathwise-noise limitations remain.

D1.justification: The new applications include hyperparameter tables specifying 100 states, 2,000 iterations, Adam at 10^-3, and Heun steps of 10^-2, alongside stimulus timing and interpolation details. S8 also newly states that Jupyter notebooks are provided; their accessibility is not established by the supplied PDFs.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations on learned Riemannian geometry and working-memory dynamics, plus references supporting chaos and the new applications. The existing positioning against static representations and fixed-point-based analyses remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The main narrative and section order remain intact. v2 appends S8.5–S8.6, expands S7.2, and makes localized grammatical and caption corrections rather than extensively rewriting the document.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figures S10–S11 and two hyperparameter tables. It also adjusts a connector in Figure 3 and coordinate annotations in Figure 5, while appendix material reflows. Existing result figures and table structures are otherwise preserved.

improvement.justification: The added task and human-data examples broaden empirical support, and S7.2 clarifies applicability without disrupting the existing evidence. These provide a limited net gain. The BCI validation remains illustrative, and the inconsistent subtraction-metric derivation in S8.5 weakens that new mechanism argument, limiting the improvement.
